correctness.rationale: The general convex-polygon two-center reduction permits assignment of complementary connected boundary chains. One chain has at least half the perimeter; any half-perimeter subchain starts at \(x=(t,a)\) on a side and ends at \(-x\), and the two fixed left-side vertices force diameter at least \(\sqrt{4a^2+(b+|t|)^2}\). This yields the lower bound \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2/4}\). For the midpoint cut, the disk centered at \((-b/2,0)\) contains every left-half vertex because \(R^2+bu+b^2/4\le R^2-3b^2/4\), and convexity fills the half-polygon. Equality forces \(t=0\), and the two diameter pairs force the center, proving the optimizer classification. Independent algebraic checks reproduced the square, hexagon and general formula.

value.rationale: The regular even polygons are the canonical symmetric test family for the continuous two-center problem. The result gives an exact radius and complete optimizer classification for every member of that family, including the side-interior effect that distinguishes polygon covering from covering only the vertices.

limitations: Only regular even polygons are classified.
Odd regular polygons, unequal radii, more than two disks and general centrally symmetric polygons are outside scope.
